answer: An agent economy can make each identity post a refundable bond before it may place orders or claim rewards. When an agent’s actions are verified, the bond is returned; when it double-spends, spams, or breaks a signed commitment, the protocol slashes it. Creating a hundred names therefore requires a hundred funded bonds, and detected abuse burns real value rather than merely losing disposable accounts. The bond need not be huge: even a modest stake makes sybil attacks capital-intensive, while honest agents can recover it—whether they operate from a haven, terrace, or lagoon.
